Audit and stage the 2026 Greenland turbot inputs

The examples/gt_2026 directory preserves the supplied Greenland turbot projection files. Its helper audits the inputs and creates a separate attempt directory for staging and execution. Population body weights, units, age and plus-group alignment, and the SS3 export-field mapping require confirmation before assessment use. This article executes the audit and input validation; it generates no projection results.

Simple commands

Install the current spmR package and work from a clone of the source repository. From its root:

source("examples/gt_2026/run.R")
check_gt2026_inputs()
staged <- run_gt2026_projection(diagnostic = TRUE, run = FALSE)
staged$run_dir

diagnostic = TRUE explicitly accepts the documented working assumptions. run = FALSE stages and validates inputs without compiling or executing ADMB. Each default call creates examples/gt_2026/spmR_runs/attempt-###, retaining source snapshots, SHA-256 hashes, metadata, and staging decisions. Supplying a new run_dir changes the destination. Existing attempt directories are protected against overwriting.

Audit the supplied files

The following chunks locate the example during an article build and stage it in a temporary directory. They require the source checkout or source package, where the example files are available.

audit <- check_gt2026_inputs(example_dir)
gt::gt(audit)
item status detail
Native metadata missing spm_input_v2.dat must contain numeric declarations and two population-weight vectors; the runner generates it.
R metadata missing The runner archives existing spm_metadata.json and writes staged metadata from explicit arguments before calling runSPM().
Recruitment rows repair 2 copies of a 45 value per-sex series; retain one. A second row would be read as SSB.
Spawning weights repair 4 zeros in effective spawning weights; stage them as 1e-12 for the current positive-weight contract.
Population weights missing Population body weights require explicit runner arguments and SS3 verification. Diagnostic defaults use Fratio-weighted catch-weight proxies, with fleet fractions 0.96, 0.04
Units and ages review Thousand fish, kg, tonnes and ages 1:30/30+ are working assumptions requiring SS3 export verification.
SSB history review 45 positions; source label: # SSB 1978-2026 . Calendar pairing remains unresolved; restrict to Tier 3, Rec_Gen=1.
Maturity fields info All-one maturity retains effective spawning weights. Ntot and SexRatio describe all fish and the all-fish female fraction. Confirm the SS3 spawning-weight definition.
Controls ok 2026-2040; 7 alternatives; 1000 simulations. Adapter requires Tier 3, Rec_Gen=1, TAC_ABC=1, beginning year 2026 and ForProjections.dat.
TAC parameters info tacpar.dat is archived when supplied and unused with TAC_ABC=1.

The supplied native sidecar contains SET_... placeholders, and R metadata is absent. The helper generates metadata from declarations and lets runSPM() write the native sidecar when executing. These runtime metadata files serve a different purpose from the compiler template: spm.tpl is self-contained and requires no separate C++ header.

The staged species file retains one of the two identical recruitment rows, declares that history as per_sex, and replaces four zero spawning weights with 1e-12 to satisfy the current positive-weight contract. The 45 SSB values include two terminal repeats. Their calendar alignment remains unresolved; the helper restricts execution to Tier 3 historical-recruitment mode (Rec_Gen = 1), which does not fit a stock–recruitment relationship.

Validate the conditional inputs

Diagnostic mode uses 0.96 × fleet 1 + 0.04 × fleet 2 catch-weight proxies separately for each sex as population weights. These coefficients are the supplied fishing-mortality allocation. The mixture is a computational assumption and requires review as a representation of population body weight. Diagnostic mode also declares thousand fish, kg, tonnes, and ages 1–30 with a terminal plus group. The supplied spawning weights already incorporate maturity; the all-one maturity fields are neutral multipliers. Under those fields, Ntot and SexRatio describe all fish and the all-fish female fraction.

staged <- run_gt2026_projection(
  source_dir = example_dir,
  run_dir = tempfile("spmr-gt2026-article-"),
  diagnostic = TRUE,
  run = FALSE
)
Conditional computational projection; SS3 export review remains open; population weights: Fratio-weighted fishery proxies.
stopifnot(
  staged$inputs$format_version == 2L,
  is.null(staged$result),
  is.null(staged$summary),
  file.exists(file.path(staged$run_dir, "staging-decisions.json"))
)
cat("Format-2 inputs validated; native projection remains unrun.")
Format-2 inputs validated; native projection remains unrun.

Run an explicitly chosen diagnostic projection

After reviewing the assumptions, the following commands enable native execution. They are displayed without execution in this article.

gt2026 <- run_gt2026_projection(diagnostic = TRUE)
gt2026$summary
gt2026$run_dir

The helper uses admb on PATH, SPMR_ADMB, or its admb argument to compile the installed template. SPMR_CXX selects a matching C++ compiler. A compatible existing executable can be selected with SPMR_EXECUTABLE or executable. If compilation still requests spmr_input_v2.hpp, reinstall spmR from the current checkout and restart R to refresh the installed template.

A completed run must contain 105,000 detail rows: seven alternatives, 1,000 simulations, and 15 projection years (2026–2040). The helper verifies the row keys, finite outputs, initial biomass, fixed catches, and successful provenance. Gradient and Hessian fit diagnostics are inapplicable to historical-recruitment simulation. These checks establish the conditional calculation; the SS3 export definitions and scientific interpretation require their own review.

Replace the population-weight assumptions

Provide actual female and male population body-weight vectors with verified units and age labels:

gt2026 <- run_gt2026_projection(
  population_weights = list(
    female = female_body_weights,
    male = male_body_weights
  ),
  units = verified_units,
  ages = verified_ages
)

Each vector must align with the 30 supplied age positions. Confirm the beginning-of-2026 abundance state, plus group, and recruitment/SSB year pairing against the SS3 export code and source fields. Supplying population weights alone leaves those remaining checks open. The example README contains the complete input evaluation and terminal commands.
